answer: Persistent Task Divergence Tracking. Each agent identity must wander through a distinct sequence of assigned micro-tasks, and the system records a behavioral fingerprint at every inlet of the pipeline. New identities draw tasks from different regions of the orchard of available work, so a duplicate agent copying one identity’s history reveals itself as two accounts producing correlated fingerprints. An attacker must maintain genuinely divergent task histories per identity, paying continuous compute and coordination cost.
